sourceOccurrences.label: Displacement kernels and translation-invariant model bounds
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 40, 49, 59, 67, 77, 85, 93, 104, 111, 118
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected statement correspondence with scope qualifications
sourceOccurrences.note: The source uses an additive group without assuming commutativity; its y-x convention is the multiplicative y x^{-1} convention in U8CI. Kernel descent and deterministic row identities do not need countability; the article states a countable context because its probability applications do. R01V gives the row identity and total-mass upper bound. The probability and intensity applications include the source bounds from a finite total-mass majorant and explain the stronger off-diagonal version separately. Each point mass sums to one, so the two-point kernel has mass two even when its two support points coincide. The source axis witness is the displayed two-point example on an integer lattice, not the full nearest-neighbour kernel. Conjugacy criteria and Euclidean power-tail estimates are expository additions, not statements of this source module.

sourceOccurrences.label: Closed gaps, crossing products and the positive-cut criterion
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with a separate ergodic consequence
sourceOccurrences.note: BQ44 groups the product identity and its three positivity/vanishing cases. The preceding argument covers the deterministic barrier and finite trapping, measurable cuts, injective crossing-pair parametrization and arbitrary-profile product. QH7Q supplies the general countable closed-coordinate formula. The source homogeneous profile specifies p(0); the article extends to arbitrary diagonal marginals because cuts ignore them. ZH13 is an additional deduction using WUAF, not a theorem exported by this module. The no-cut subcritical example is also additional; absence of cuts is not equated with percolation.

sourceOccurrences.note: FQCZ supplies exact balls and shells, their sharper and weaker bounds, and the extended radial sum identity. 6VNM retains the origin convention, all real exponents, positive dimension, scalar power-series and finite telescoping contracts, both finite-sum and extended-sum interpretations, and the inclusive tail constant. B2ZL remains unchanged with its strict cutoff and separate constants. The zero-dimensional exception is explicit.

sourceOccurrences.label: Zero rooted and global critical intensities
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit endpoint conventions
sourceOccurrences.note: K38T uses the existing displacement row identity and independent degree criterion. The source works on an additive group without a commutativity assumption and exports the two threshold equalities. The article also spells out their infinite-degree mechanism at each positive intensity, with simultaneity over countably many vertices and a separate zero-intensity endpoint.

sourceOccurrences.relationship: Source-inspected exposition with explicit scope distinctions
sourceOccurrences.note: The source includes diagonal values in its translation and radial hypotheses. The article separates the diagonal-erasure extension, preserves the single probability-one event for all vertices, and treats root and global thresholds as extended infima over finite intensities.

proofUses.reason: Injectively enumerate crossing pairs and apply the countable closed-product law; logarithmic estimates give the exact positivity criterion.
Positive cut probability and ergodicity exclude an empty cut set; stationarity excludes an extremal cut, and deterministic barriers trap every cluster.
Shell grouping reduces the kernel to a scalar power series and retains the inclusive boundary shell in the tail.
The displacement row identity and a truncation lower bound make each probability row infinite; independent degrees give the threshold conclusion.
Direct algebra of displacements under swapping and translation; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
Reindexing by the bijection y -> yx^{-1}; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
Shell counting and integral comparison of the power series; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
The conditional product law of the unrevealed cross bonds gives exact formulas, bounded by elementary scalar inequalities; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
Riemann-sum convergence of the intensities and a Bernoulli-Poisson coupling; no other wiki assertion is invoked.
